name: The Athenian naval empire
plain_explanation: Athens turned a voluntary defensive alliance against Persia into an empire by letting most member states pay money instead of supplying ships, which gave Athens the cash and navy to dominate its former allies.
precise_definition: The transformation of the Delian League, whose constitution required member states to contribute ships or their cash equivalent, into an instrument of Athenian naval hegemony once most states chose the cash option.
why_it_mattered: This imperial wealth, not native Athenian genius alone, is what Russell credits with making the cultural explosion materially possible.
historical_origin: Formed after the Persian Wars to liberate and protect the Ionian Greeks.
connection_to_politics_or_religion: Directly bound up with Pericles's imperialist policy, which Russell says produced increasing friction with Sparta.
